item.title: Gut Microbiota Links to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
item.description: A systematic review reveals how gut microbiota changes, inflammation, and intestinal barrier dysfunction may influence benign prostatic hyperplasia development. The post Gut Microbiota Links to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Fecal Metabolites Linked to Crohn’s Disease Progression
item.description: Fecal metabolites interact with gut microbes in Crohn’s disease, revealing signals that could guide new treatments and dietary strategies. The post Fecal Metabolites Linked to Crohn’s Disease Progression appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Mediterranean Diet Linked to Lower Stroke Risk in Women
item.description: Long-term data from California Teachers Study show higher adherence to the Mediterranean diet is linked to reduced risk of stroke in women. The post Mediterranean Diet Linked to Lower Stroke Risk in Women appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Gut Microbiota Dysbiosis is a Factor in Diabetic Retinopathy
item.description: Gut microbiota dysbiosis might contribute to the development of diabetic retinopathy through the gut-eye axis, according to a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis. The post Gut Microbiota Dysbiosis is a Factor in Diabetic Retinopathy appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Kidney Function Linked to Elevated Alzheimer’s Blood Biomarkers
item.description: A large meta-analysis links reduced kidney function to higher Alzheimer’s disease blood biomarkers, suggesting renal health may affect interpretation of dementia tests. The post Kidney Function Linked to Elevated Alzheimer’s Blood Biomarkers appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: COPD Exacerbation Risk Spikes After Stopping LAMA or ICS
item.description: Stopping LAMA or ICS in COPD, raised exacerbation risk for three months, with pronounced withdrawal-associated spikes. The post COPD Exacerbation Risk Spikes After Stopping LAMA or ICS appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy Improves Outcomes in Pulmonary Embolism
item.description: STORM-PE shows that mechanical thrombectomy leads to greater early improvement in right ventricular function than anticoagulation alone in intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism, without increased major adverse events. The post Mechanical Thrombectomy Improves Outcomes in Pulmonary Embolism appeared first on European Medical Journal.

item.title: Rare disease access remains uneven across the US
item.description: A new report has found that for Americans living with rare conditions, access to the latest innovations depends on their zip code. The post Rare disease access remains uneven across the US appeared first on European Medical Journal.
